newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen dipping slightly at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen dipping slightly at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly lower Thursday, with the Dow industrials extending yesterday's losses amid profit-taking and a softer bond market.
But larger-capitalization technology stocks were expected to fare better, following above-forecast results from Compaq Computer Corp, and this will ultimately help the broader market, analysts said.
"We could see a slight slippage at the open, though nothing too serious," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was down 3.60 points at 914.40 and the long bond lost 9/32 to yield 6.59 percent. Both declined from earlier levels following news of a stronger-than-forecast rise in new jobless claims.
Initial jobless claims for the week ended July 5 rose to 377,000 from 337,000 in the previous week. A rise of 341,000 had been forecast.
Compaq reported second quarter earnings of $1.48 per share -- above the First Call estimate of $1.39 but below the so-called "whisper" number of $1.50.
"Whisper" numbers refer to unpublished earnings estimates that circulate on Wall Street just ahead of earnings reports.
"The tech stocks are tough to call here," Ackerman said.
Seagate Technology Inc reported below-forecast earnings of $0.61 per share, excluding charges, compared to $0.52 per share, without charges, a year earlier.
Apple Computer Corp was expected to move down after news that Chairman Gilbert Amelio had resigned, analysts said.
